click-test.a1: CPS means clicks per second. Click the pad as fast as you can until the time runs out; your clicks are divided by the seconds of the test.
click-test.a2: Most people click 5–8 times a second with one finger. 8–11 is fast, and above 11 usually takes jitter or butterfly clicking.
click-test.q3: Which test length should I pick?
click-test.a3: 5 seconds is the usual test. 1 second measures a short burst; 30 and 60 seconds show how well you keep the pace.
click-test.a4: Yes: with the pad focused, each press of Space or Enter counts once. Holding the key down does not repeat.
click-test.a5: Your best score for each length is shown until you close the tab. Nothing is uploaded or stored.

reaction-time.q1: How does the reaction time test work?
reaction-time.a1: Click the pad to start. It turns red; after a random 1.5–4.5 seconds it turns green. Click as soon as you see green. The time between green and your click is your reaction time.
reaction-time.q2: What is a normal reaction time?
reaction-time.a2: Most people react to a visual signal in about 200–300 ms with a mouse or touch screen. Under 200 ms is fast.
reaction-time.a3: Single tries vary a lot. The average and median of five give a steadier number; the best and worst are shown too.
reaction-time.q4: Does my device change the result?
reaction-time.a4: Yes. Screen refresh, mouse or touch latency and browser load add a few to tens of milliseconds, so compare results on the same device.
reaction-time.q5: What if I click too early?
reaction-time.a5: Clicking while the pad is red shows “Too soon” and the try does not count. Click again to retry it.

tone-generator.q1: What can I use a tone generator for?
tone-generator.a1: To test speakers and headphones, check left and right channels, find a rattle or hum, tune an instrument to A4 = 440 Hz, or try the range of your hearing.
tone-generator.a2: Sine is a pure tone, best for tests. Square, triangle and sawtooth add harmonics and sound buzzier.
tone-generator.q3: Why can't I hear very low or very high tones?
tone-generator.a3: Small speakers rarely play below about 80 Hz, and hearing above 15–17 kHz fades with age. Your device's audio path may cut them too.
tone-generator.q4: Is it safe for my ears and speakers?
tone-generator.a4: Start at a low volume, especially with headphones and high frequencies. Volume starts at 20% for that reason. Stop if it hurts.
tone-generator.a5: The tone is made in your browser with Web Audio; once the page has loaded, nothing else is downloaded or uploaded.

tally-counter.a1: Press + or − on a counter, or use the keyboard: Space, ↑ or + adds, ↓ or − subtracts on the highlighted counter.
tally-counter.a2: Yes. Add up to 12 counters, give each a name and see the total of all of them.
tally-counter.q3: Can I count by more than one?
tally-counter.a3: Set the step (1–1000). Each press then adds or subtracts that amount.
tally-counter.a4: Yes, in this browser only (local storage). They come back when you reopen the page; private windows may forget them.
tally-counter.q5: Can the count go below zero?
tally-counter.a5: Only if you tick “Allow negative numbers”. Otherwise counters stop at 0.

mic-test.q1: How do I test my microphone?
mic-test.a1: Press Start microphone and allow access. Speak: the meter and waveform should move. Record 5 seconds and play it back to hear how you sound.
mic-test.q2: The meter does not move. What now?
mic-test.a2: Pick another device in the list, check that the microphone is not muted (some headsets have a switch), and close other apps that use it. On a laptop, check the system's input volume.
mic-test.a3: Speech peaks around −20 to −6 dBFS are good. Near 0 dBFS the sound clips; below −20 it is quiet.
mic-test.a4: No. The audio and the test recording stay in this tab and are gone when you close it.
mic-test.q5: Why does the browser ask for permission?
mic-test.a5: Browsers only give a page the microphone after you allow it. You can take the permission back in the site settings at any time.

click-test.lead: Measure how many times you can click per second. Nothing is uploaded.
click-test.s1b: The test length is 5 seconds by default. Pick 1, 10, 30 or 60 seconds in Length.
click-test.s2b: The timer starts with your first click. Click as fast as you can; clicks and CPS update live.
click-test.s3b: When time runs out you get your CPS and total clicks. Your best score for each length is kept until you close the tab.

reaction-time.lead: Measure your visual reaction time in milliseconds. Nothing is uploaded.
reaction-time.s1b: Click the pad to start a try.
reaction-time.s2b: The pad turns red. Do not click yet; clicking too soon does not count.
reaction-time.s3b: Click as soon as it turns green. After five tries you see the average, median, best and worst.

tone-generator.lead: Play a pure tone at any frequency from 20 Hz to 20 kHz. Nothing is uploaded.
tone-generator.s1b: It is set to 440 Hz (A4), a sine wave, both speakers, at 20% volume. Press Play.
tone-generator.s2b: Type a value, drag the slider, use ÷2/×2 for an octave or pick a preset such as 1000 Hz.
tone-generator.s3b: Pick a waveform and send the tone to the left, right or both speakers to test them one at a time.

tally-counter.lead: Count anything with big buttons or the keyboard. Counts are kept in this browser.
tally-counter.s1b: One counter starts at 0. Give it a name if you like.
tally-counter.s2b: Press + to add and − to subtract, or use Space, ↑ and ↓ on the keyboard.
tally-counter.s3b: Press Add counter to count several things at once; the total of all counters is shown underneath.

mic-test.lead: Check that your microphone works and how it sounds. Nothing is uploaded.
mic-test.s1b: Press Start microphone and allow access when the browser asks.
mic-test.s2b: The level meter and waveform move with your voice. Aim for peaks between −20 and −6 dBFS.
mic-test.s3b: Press Record 5 s, speak, then play the recording to hear how the microphone itself sounds, before any call app filters.
